transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I've been having a really hard time with constantly fidgeting and feeling restless. I just can't seem to sit still, and I'm always tapping my hands or feet.
Along with the restlessness, do you also have trouble paying attention or staying organized, or is it more that you feel constantly worried or on edge? Which of those fits you better most days?

I definitely struggle more with paying attention and staying organized rather than feeling worried or anxious. I find myself constantly avoiding or putting off any tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort because they feel so overwhelming to start. It’s not really that I feel on edge, I just really dislike and avoid things that need that kind of deep focus.
Besides the fidgeting, do you often act before thinking, interrupt people, or have trouble waiting your turn? Or is it mostly the inattention and disorganization without those impulsive behaviors?

Yes, I definitely do that—I often find myself blurting out answers before someone has even finished asking their question. It is really a mix of both types of issues, because I also struggle with and tend to avoid any tasks that require sustained mental effort.
Have these attention and impulsivity problems been present since childhood, like before age 12, or did they start later in life?
Yes, they've definitely been present since I was a kid. I remember struggling with these exact same things back in elementary school, well before I was 12 years old.
Do these symptoms cause problems in more than one part of your life, like both at work or school and at home or in relationships? Can you tell me if they show up across those different settings?
To be honest, I'm not quite sure. I haven't really thought about how they affect different areas of my life like work or home specifically.
Can you think of specific examples of these symptoms causing trouble in at least two settings, such as work or school, home, or relationships?
I'm really not sure, to be honest. I haven't thought about it enough to divide it up by settings like that, so I can't think of specific examples for home versus work.
Overall, how much do these symptoms interfere with your daily life—would you say mildly, moderately, or severely?
I'm not quite sure how to rate it, and I haven't really thought about it in those exact terms. I just know that dealing with all of this has been a persistent struggle for me.
Thinking back over the past 6 months, would you say your problems are mainly with inattention, mainly with hyperactivity and impulsivity, or clearly both about equally?

I feel like it is clearly a mix of both. I really struggle with staying focused and avoiding tasks that require a lot of mental effort, while also constantly feeling restless, fidgeting, and blurting out answers before people finish speaking.
Even if it’s hard to sort by setting, have these symptoms caused noticeable problems with responsibilities or relationships in at least two areas of life, such as work or school and home?
I'm still not quite sure about that. I haven't really thought about whether these issues have caused problems across different areas like work or home specifically.
What is one concrete problem these symptoms have caused recently, like missing deadlines, losing things, interrupting others, or trouble sitting through meetings?

I frequently interrupt people by blurting out answers before they can even finish asking their questions. I also really struggle to sit still during meetings, constantly fidgeting and tapping my hands and feet the whole time.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports clinically significant symptoms from both ADHD domains: inattention (difficulty paying attention/staying organized, avoidance of tasks requiring sustained mental effort) and hyperactivity/impulsivity (restlessness, inability to sit still, fidgeting, blurting out answers). Symptoms were present since childhood before age 12 and have persisted over at least the past 6 months. Combined presentation is favored because both symptom clusters are clearly endorsed, though cross-setting impairment was not fully established in the interview.
